subsystems.name: Atmosphere intake
subsystems.role: supplies carbon dioxide from the thin Martian air.

subsystems.name: Water supply
subsystems.role: provides the hydrogen and part of the oxygen the plant needs.

subsystems.name: Methanation reactor
subsystems.role: runs the Sabatier step, making methane and water from carbon dioxide and hydrogen.

subsystems.name: Electrolysis
subsystems.role: splits water into hydrogen and oxygen, and can also split carbon dioxide.

subsystems.name: Liquefaction and storage
subsystems.role: chills methane and oxygen to liquid and keeps them liquid.

subsystems.name: Power and thermal control
subsystems.role: the plant must run continuously for years without a crew.
parts: fission surface power unit or solar arrays

subsystems.name: Autonomous control
subsystems.role: the plant must make propellant before anyone arrives to run it.

buildSteps.title: Send a robotic precursor
buildSteps.detail: Land the power source and plant hardware years ahead of any crew, at a site with accessible ice and near the planned return vehicle.

buildSteps.title: Capture and clean carbon dioxide
buildSteps.detail: Compress the thin atmosphere, filter out dust, and freeze out water vapour so the gas fed to the reactor is mostly CO2.

buildSteps.title: Mine and purify water ice
buildSteps.detail: Drill or dig into subsurface ice, sublimate it to vapour, condense it, and remove salts and dust.

buildSteps.title: Make hydrogen and oxygen by electrolysis
buildSteps.detail: Split purified water into hydrogen and oxygen; most hydrogen goes to the reactor and the oxygen is stored.

buildSteps.title: Run the Sabatier reactor
buildSteps.detail: Pass carbon dioxide and hydrogen over a catalyst at a few hundred degrees Celsius and moderate pressure to make methane and water; recycle the water back to electrolysis.

buildSteps.title: Make extra oxygen from carbon dioxide
buildSteps.detail: Run solid-oxide electrolysis of CO2 to produce carbon monoxide and more oxygen, topping up the oxygen supply.

buildSteps.title: Liquefy and store the propellant
buildSteps.detail: Cool methane to about −162 °C and oxygen to about −183 °C and hold them in insulated tanks with boil-off recovery.

buildSteps.title: Prime the return vehicle
buildSteps.detail: Transfer propellant to the ascent vehicle, verify purity against engine requirements, and keep the plant running autonomously through the launch window.

prerequisites.why: carbon dioxide reduction units have run for years on the International Space Station, though at life-support rather than propellant scale.
oxygen generators on spacecraft and submarines already split water reliably.
a small instrument on a Mars rover produced oxygen from atmospheric CO2 in 2021, proving the chemistry on site but at tiny scale.
orbiters and landers have mapped shallow ice, but no mission has yet mined and processed it.
small reactors have been ground-tested, but none has flown or operated on another planet.
a propellant plant must run for thousands of hours with no crew, handling dust, cold and faults on its own.

pathway.milestone: small flight demonstrations and laboratory rigs proving each step separately
pathway.unlocks: confidence that the core chemistry works in the Martian environment.

pathway.milestone: a robotic lander that mines ice and runs an integrated plant at pilot scale
pathway.unlocks: real numbers for yield, dust tolerance and reliability.

pathway.milestone: a full-scale plant that fills a return vehicle's tanks before its crew leaves Earth
pathway.unlocks: a far smaller mission mass, which is what makes crewed Mars missions practical.

pathway.milestone: stored propellant depots and refuelling, including in orbit
pathway.unlocks: reusable interplanetary transport and support for a permanent surface base.
